false_positives.candidate:
Strategy close() shuts down the factory-shared queue pool, breaking later partition assignments
The FixedQueuePool is created once in the factory __init__ and shared by every strategy that create_with_partitions builds. Arroyo closes and joins the old strategy on a rebalance, then creates a new one. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown and shuts the queues down. The factory still holds the dead pool, so the new strategy submits to shut-down queues. put() raises queue.ShutDown, submit() catches it, and the except branch marks the offset complete. Messages are then committed without ever being processed.

Offsets committed from a background thread instead of the arroyo consumer thread
The commit function handed to the strategy is arroyo's Commit callable. It touches StreamProcessor/consumer state that is only meant to be used from the main poll thread. _commit_loop calls it from a separate daemon thread, concurrently with poll() and the consumer's own commit handling. Arroyo's strategies call commit from submit/poll only. The commit thread can race with rebalance handling and with the Kafka consumer, which is not thread-safe, and can commit offsets for partitions that have already been revoked.

No backpressure: queues are unbounded
The docstring claims natural backpressure, but queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit() never blocks or raises MessageRejected. If workers are slower than Kafka consumption, memory grows without limit and many uncommitted messages pile up.

OffsetTracker state persists across rebalances
The tracker is owned by the factory-wide shared pool, but a new strategy is created on every partition assignment. last_committed, all_offsets and outstanding are never reset or pruned on revoke. If a partition is revoked and later reassigned, possibly after another consumer committed a different position, the stale last_committed makes `start` skip offsets. Stale outstanding/all_offsets entries from revoked partitions can also block or mis-order commits.

Offset gaps stall commits permanently and leak memory
get_committable_offsets only advances through contiguous offsets that were submitted. Kafka offsets can legitimately be missing (transaction markers, compaction). One missing offset makes the loop break forever, so no later offset is committed. all_offsets grows without bound, and range(start, max_offset+1) is rescanned every second.
